name: Miami Chase Rule Pursuit
formation: Pro Set Wing Sweep Right vs Even Speed Front
coverage: Cover 3 Sky with run-fit chase rules

summary.motive: Turn perimeter runs into short gains by having all eleven defenders execute assigned pursuit angles rather than chasing the football.
summary.keyDefender: The strong safety filling the alley as the second hat
summary.whyItWorks: Every defender has a geometric landmark instead of a ball target, so the convergence point forms ahead of the runner regardless of how fast the play gets to the edge.
summary.failureMode: A single defender breaks his landmark and chases the ball, opening the cutback lane the cross-facing Will is counting on him to erase.

beats.title: 1. The Chase Rule Declares
beats.text: The moment sweep flow shows, every defender executes a pre-assigned pursuit rule — the backside end runs down the line of scrimmage through the tailback’s original spot, not to the football.

beats.title: 2. Spill Forces Width
beats.text: The playside tackle spills the drive block and the end holds the edge, forcing the ball carrier wider than his intended landmark and directly toward waiting pursuit angles.

beats.title: 3. Three Angles, One Point
beats.text: Sam takes the inside-out angle from the box, Mike runs deeper than the ball through the guard’s original alignment, and the corner locks inside-out force at the numbers.

beats.title: 4. The Miami Swarm
beats.text: Five defenders converge at one coordinate from five different angles, tackling with shared responsibility exactly as Jimmy Johnson taught at Miami — pursuit is a system, not effort.

relations.tell: The backside end takes visibly flat steps down the line of scrimmage instead of angling upfield — the chase rule targets a spot, not the runner.
